issues.legal_issue: On the death of a tenant, the tenancy devolves on the heirs as a single joint tenancy unless succession is excluded or limited.
material_facts: The original tenant died, leaving heirs who inherited the tenancy.
The tenancy remained a single tenancy, with no division of the premises or of the rent payable.
issues.conclusion: The heirs succeeded to the tenancy as joint tenants, not as tenants in common.
issues.legal_principle: The Court held that, absent a provision excluding or limiting succession, the tenancy devolves on the heirs with the same incidence as it had for the original tenant; it remains a single tenancy without division of the premises or rent. The Court affirmed Shrimati Vishnawati v. Bhagwat Vithu Chowdhry, [1969] A.L.J. 1131, and overruled Ramesh Chand Bose v. Gopeshwar Prasad Sharma, AIR 1977 Allahabad 38.

rule.if: original_tenant_died and heirs_succeeded_to_tenancy and no_succession_exclusion_or_limit and tenancy_remained_undivided

predicates.original_tenant_died: The person who held the tenancy died.
predicates.heirs_succeeded_to_tenancy: The deceased tenant's heirs succeeded to the tenancy.
predicates.no_succession_exclusion_or_limit: No applicable provision excluded or limited the heirs' succession to the tenancy.
predicates.tenancy_remained_undivided: The tenancy remained single, without division of the premises or the rent payable.

issues.definition: When the original tenant dies and the heirs succeed to an undivided tenancy without succession being excluded or limited, the heirs succeed as joint tenants.

issues.legal_issue: A notice terminating an inherited single tenancy may be effective when served on one coheir who acts on behalf of the other heirs.
material_facts: The respondent inherited the tenancy with the original tenant's other heirs.
The landlord served the termination notice on the respondent alone and brought an ejectment suit against him.
The respondent paid rent on behalf of the other heirs and accepted the notice on their behalf.
issues.conclusion: The notice served on the respondent was valid, and the ejectment suit could succeed.
issues.legal_principle: Under section 106 of the Transfer of Property Act, 1882, the notice served on the respondent was sufficient in these circumstances because the heirs held a single tenancy as joint tenants and the respondent acted on their behalf. The Court affirmed Shrimati Vishnawati v. Bhagwat Vithu Chowdhry, [1969] A.L.J. 1131, and rejected the contrary view in Ramesh Chand Bose v. Gopeshwar Prasad Sharma, AIR 1977 Allahabad 38.

rule.if: ejectment_proceeding and inherited_single_tenancy and termination_notice_served_on_one_heir and recipient_acted_for_all_heirs

predicates.ejectment_proceeding: A landlord brought a proceeding to recover possession after seeking to terminate a tenancy.
predicates.inherited_single_tenancy: Heirs inherited one undivided tenancy from a deceased tenant.
predicates.termination_notice_served_on_one_heir: The landlord served the termination notice on one heir rather than separately on every heir.
predicates.recipient_acted_for_all_heirs: The heir who received the notice acted for the other heirs, including by paying rent on their behalf and accepting the notice on their behalf.

issues.definition: In an ejectment proceeding, service of a termination notice on one heir is valid when the heirs inherited a single tenancy and the recipient acted for them all.
